newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa climbs up but still within range.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa climbs up but still within range.

text.p: Trade buying kept London cocoa futures bubbling above 1,030 stg on Wednesday after strong gains but there was little inspiration to push the market through nearby resistance, traders said.

The May contract initially jumped to 1,035 stg per tonne but spent most of the session below 1,030 as sterling's gains against the dollar put renewed pressure. The benchmark position ended 14 stg up on the day at 1,030.
Chart analysts say it needs to overcome the 1,035-40 area to secure a hike to the recent seven-month peak of 1,048 and challenge the congestion around 1,050.
But the latest bounce at least staved off a critical test of support below 989 that threatened to push May down to 950, traders said.
"It's still within the range but it seems to be finding good support," said one trader.
Turnover reached 8,720 lots but included some 4,500 lots of May/Dec crossed by Mees Pierson.
"There isn't any real interest," said the trader.
Mees Pierson, MHF Futures, Credit Lyonnais and SFH were said to be the day's main buyers, although Phibro, believed to be holding long physical stocks, could also have been involved.
"It looks as though it decided to put some orders round the market," said the trader.

Forecasts of thundershowers in the Ivory Coast for the weekend injected negative sentiment as they improved prospects for the midcrop but traders are now betting on strong first quarter grind data to give the market fresh momentum.
"People also think what's the point of selling if the Phibro position is going to be a problem," said one.
Wednesday's deals saw the structure tighten across the board with May/July trading at 9-10 stg, May/Sept at 15 and Sept/Dec at 14-15.
The May contract needed to reassert itself above 1,040 stg on Thursday but much depended on New York's performance and the level of sterling, traders said.
"The problem is all the traders ran off to coffee," said one.
Thursday is the last session before the market closes for Easter holiday until Tuesday.
